_comment: LTX-2.3's own prompt enhancer. Gemma-3-12B is already loaded as LTX's text encoder, so the abliterated LoRA turns that SAME resident model into a chat LLM that rewrites your one-liner into the dense shot description LTX actually wants. TextGenerateLTX2Prompt has LTX's house style baked into its system prompt - camera move, subject motion, ambience, lighting - which is exactly the structure a video model needs and an image-prompt LLM does not produce.
_notes: This is what models/loras/gemma-3-12b-it-abliterated_lora_rank64_bf16.safetensors is for. It is NOT an image LoRA and does nothing to the picture - it is applied to the TEXT ENCODER so the encoder will write prompts instead of refusing or moralising about them. Abliteration removes refusal directions; it does not make the video model do anything new.

LoraLoader needs BOTH a model and a clip. The MODEL output (node 4[0]) is discarded here - only the CLIP output (node 4[1]) is used. That is why node 3 exists: it supplies a MODEL just to satisfy the input.
strength_clip=1.0 is the one that matters. strength_model=1.0 is inert in this graph.
Zero extra VRAM cost when chained onto an LTX render: Gemma-3-12B is already resident as the text encoder. Standalone, expect ~9.4 GB and a slower first run while it loads.

TextGenerateLTX2Prompt vs TextGenerate (workflow 15): same node family, different built-in system prompt. Use THIS one for video and workflow 15's for stills. Do not cross them - an image prompt fed to LTX produces a static shot, because it never mentions motion.
sampling_mode sub-inputs must be dotted keys ('sampling_mode.temperature'). See workflow 15's notes.
max_length 2048 matches the official template. These descriptions run long on purpose - LTX does not degrade on long prompts the way SDXL-era models did.
To chain: take the STRING from node 5 and link it into node 10's `text` in workflow 17, exactly the way workflow 16 links its LLM into CLIPTextEncode.

inputs.prompt: a brass diving helmet on wet stone at the tide line
